goal: Add atomic bulk SOCKS residential management with exact unique names, selected/all delete and credential export; implement real per-connection health-aware distributed routing biased toward the fastest healthy endpoints.
context: Keep exact geosite:google@ads plus temporary domain:browserleaks.com, direct cached IPv4 DNS, UDP and all client/profile/generation/account policies. Existing router chooses one endpoint even when down. Use native Xray local burst observatory (10s interval, 1 sample, 3s timeout), leastLoad known-alive selection, fail-closed blackhole fallback, 80 percent fast lane and 20 percent all-healthy exploration via random loopback lanes; separate SOCKS-only UDP candidates. No probe observation should trigger fleet Xray restarts. Unknown/unavailable endpoints receive no production traffic before local probe success. Health transitions measured using installed core fault tests including failure/recovery and distribution; latency is not bandwidth. Bound central checks concurrently and expose timestamps and observation errors. Bulk import host:port:user:password preserves password colons and exact names, offers editable preview generated from case-preserved prefix, rejects case-insensitive duplicate names and payload errors before any write. Store encrypted secrets transactionally; idempotency survives response loss; never log credentials. Bulk delete operates on explicitly confirmed IDs and preserves shared account proxies; export admin-only no-store. Never create user example endpoints or delete production fixtures. Use isolated PostgreSQL and local browser fixtures. Keep existing cross-process panel lock and content-addressed route proofs, extend verification for load-balancer loopback outcomes. Canary before full production rollout; rollback on failure.
commit_message: feat(residential): bulk SOCKS management and adaptive healthy proxy pools
